newsitem.title: USA: Penske Motorsports plans Denver-area track.
newsitem.headline: Penske Motorsports plans Denver-area track.

text.p: Penske Motorsports Inc said Tuesday it intends to seek approvals to build a new, permanent motorsports complex near the new Denver International Airport in Adams County, Colorado.

Penske said it has obtained an option agreement to purchase a 640-acre parcel for the project, located about 15 miles from downtown Denver. Financial terms of the option agreement were not disclosed, but it allows Penske to conduct customary due diligence and to engage in pre-development activities necessary to gain approval for the construction and operation of the race track.

Penske Motorsports, controlled by Detroit transportation mogul Roger Penske, owns large speedways in Brooklyn, Mich., Nazareth, Pa. and Fontana Calif., and recently obtained a majority interest in the North Carolina Motor Speedway near Rockingham, N.C.
The company also holds a 40 percent interest in Homestead-Miami Speedway in Florida and a minority interest in the Grand Prix Association of Long Beach Inc.
The company's tracks hold automobile races sponsored by both the National Association of Stock Car Racing (NASCAR) and the open-wheeled Championship Auto Racing Teams (CART).
